parcalar.metin: [excited, emphatic science storyteller] A single uranium fuel pellet, the size of a fingertip, holds about as much energy as a ton of coal! Energy Sources, episode four: the atom.
It all starts with fission. A neutron hits a uranium-235 nucleus, the nucleus splits in two, releasing heat and new neutrons.
Those neutrons split other nuclei. In a reactor, this chain reaction is kept in constant balance by control rods.
Uranium is packed into fuel rods as small ceramic pellets. The rods are grouped into bundles and placed in the reactor core.
The heat of fission warms water. In most plants, this hot water turns water in a second loop into steam.
The steam spins a turbine, and a generator makes electricity. The white cloud above cooling towers isn't smoke; it's water vapor.
The reactor runs inside a thick steel pressure vessel and a concrete containment building.
Turkey's first nuclear power plant is Akkuyu, in Mersin. When all four units are complete, its total capacity will be four thousand eight hundred megawatts.
[excited] The enormous energy inside the atom! Next episode: the heat beneath our feet. Follow Kozmos Lab.
